subtype: Approach: switching from wandering to staying and asking [Revision]
passage: Paulo had already walked two lanes of the Sunday market in Singapore's Little India, and every stall looked the same: flowers, bangles, phone covers. His family was at none of them. Each corner took him farther from where they had started, and his throat felt tight. He stopped short. "I keep moving and they keep not being here." Beside a chai stall he planted his feet, took a breath and looked up at the owner, a woman named Ada. "Please, can you call my father? I'm lost." Ada wiped her hands and picked up her phone. Paulo sat on an upturned crate and watched the crowd, this time only waiting.

qa.q: Where did Paulo stop to ask for help?
qa.a: He stopped beside a chai stall.

qa.q: What was Paulo feeling when he stopped short?
qa.a: Paulo felt anxious, his throat tight, and he realised his walking was making things worse, since each corner took him farther from his family.

qa.q: What could Paulo have done from the start, and why?
qa.a: He could have stayed near the place he last saw his family and asked a stall owner for help, because his family would come back there.

qa.q: How might Ada see Paulo's request?
qa.a: She sees a boy who asks politely and clearly, so she can act at once by picking up her phone.

grounding: A boy who wanders and makes things worse switches to staying and asking a stall owner to phone his father.
